description: Run deterministic triage on an open dispute and record the result. Triage applies fixed rules, stated here, to the dispute record: R1 (duplicate_charge) looks up the receipts the ledger counter-signed for the same seller, payer and settlement transaction hash, reading the hash only in 0x-prefixed 64-hex-digit form and the payer only in 0x-prefixed 40-hex-digit form (either letter case), and lists at most 16 of those receipts, the earliest ones and the disputed one (on a settlement of more than 16 the rationale says "more than 16 receipts" and which are listed, and adjudicationInputs carries sameSettlementTruncated: true), and classifies the disputed receipt refund when an earlier one shares that hash and uphold otherwise; R2 (not_delivered, wrong_content) classifies the claim refund when the seller filed no evidence before the evidence deadline; anything else, including a duplicate_charge receipt without a settlement transaction hash or a payer in those forms, is marked escalated with no result, for an external venue the parties choose. R1 reads receipts from one seller to one payer that share one settlement transaction as one payment. The rules never read the content, kind or note of any evidence, or the claimant's statement; no discretion and no model are involved, and the same inputs always produce the same result and rationale. The result is a triage classification recorded as data: it is not an adjudication, award or legal conclusion, it decides no legal claim, and it binds no one unless the parties separately agree. Side effects: writes the result to the dispute record, signed by the ledger; a refund result also logs a PENDING refund entry against the receipt for the claimed amount (not counter-signed into the chain; no payment is checked and no money moves). Runs once: the first successful call closes the dispute to evidence, and every later call returns 409. This tool sends no API key, so a not_delivered or wrong_content dispute can be triaged only after its evidence deadline (before it the ledger answers 409 or 401); a duplicate_charge dispute can be triaged at any time. Returns { id, status: "adjudicated" (the wire name for a dispute a rule classified) | "escalated", verdict: "refund" | "uphold" | null (the triage result), rationale (names the rule applied), adjudicationInputs (the exact inputs the rules ran on), verdictDigest, ledgerSignature, ledgerSigner, decidedAt }.

disputeDigest.description: 0x-prefixed digest of the open dispute to triage, as returned by open_dispute

name: adjudicate_dispute
